newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: LGT announces Shaw to leave Chancellor.
newsitem.headline: LGT announces Shaw to leave Chancellor.

text.p: Liechtenstein Global Trust (LGT), the Vaduz-based private banking and asset management group, said on Friday that Warren Shaw, CEO of its New York-based Chancellor LGT, will resign as part of a restructuring within the group's North American activities.

The departures followed a decision to separate management of LGT's North American retail and institutional business, LGT said. Shaw also served as global chief investment officer of LGT's asset management division.
The LGT Group is facing several changes, and challenges in its efforts to coordinate and streamline its expanding global operations, headquartered in the tiny Principality of Liechtenstein.

Besides a new CEO for Chancellor, LGT is currently looking for a group CEO to take over the role from current chairman and CEO Prince Philipp von und zu Liechtenstein, brother of reigning Liechtenstein ruler Prince Hans-Adam II.
The Prince will remain as the LGT group's chairman.

Penny Zuckerwise, Chancellor LGT's president and head of business management in North America, along with Rachel Arfa, its chief legal officer, and Jeffrey Trogone, its CFO are also leaving Chancellor.

LGT, with 127 billion Swiss francs ($83.1 billion) under management at the end of June, roughly doubled its assets after it acquired Chancellor last year, renaming it Chancellor LGT Asset Management, Inc.
LGT gained an important foothold in the U.S. institutional fund management business with the Chancellor purchase announced last summer, while Chancellor gained an international partner in LGT.
"We believe LGT was the right partner a year ago, and we believe so now," Alexandra Trower, spokeswoman for Chancellor LGT told Reuters.
Regarding the relationship with LGT, she said: "It was a perfect match, it still is a perfect match."
"There will be no change on the investment management side and no change on the client service side. This is really business management change," she said.

LGT said the move aimed to separate the management of its U.S. institutional business under Chancellor and retail business led by GT Global Investor Services, the California-based firm which also belongs to LGT.
Chancellor's North American investment team will continue as investment advisor to GT Global, Trower said.
Paul Loach, currently head of LGT's European Asset Management unit in London, will oversee U.S. institutional operations in New York as chairman of Chancellor LGT's board.
Loach has the support of the remaining team at Chancellor, one source close to the Liechtenstein operations said.
William Guilfoyle, president of GT Global, will now manage GT Global's mutual fund business in San Fransisco.
